text.L1: A fraction names equal parts of one whole.
text.L2: The bottom number tells how many equal parts make the whole, and the top number tells how many we take.
text.L3: Here, one-half has two equal parts, while one-quarter has four equal parts.
text.L4: More equal parts make smaller pieces, so one-half is bigger than one-quarter.
text.L5: That busts the myth that a bigger bottom number makes a bigger fraction.
text.L6: A fraction of a collection also means sharing the collection into equal groups.
text.L7: To find one-third of 15 pencils, share them into three equal groups.
text.L8: Each group has 5 pencils, so one-third of 15 is 5.

task.prompt: Arrange these pieces from biggest to smallest.
